Role Context

This role sits within Events Marketing. You'll help build and run MaintainX's field and events program, including regional events, user meetups, brand activations, and our flagship client-facing conference, with a mentor on the team to help you grow into owning bigger pieces of it.

The Role

You'll get hands-on with every part of our field events program, from the regional meetup down the street to the flagship conference that brings our biggest customers together, and you'll pick up real ownership fast.

 - Plan and execute regional events, user meetups, and brand activations that put MaintainX in front of the prospects and customers who matter most.

 - Build attendee lists, coordinate invites, and drive the follow-up that turns event conversations into real pipeline.

 - Own smaller events end-to-end (venue, vendor, run-of-show, the works) and dig into the flagship conference as it comes together.

 - Track what's working, like meetings booked, accounts engaged, pipeline sourced and influenced, and use that data to make the next event better than the last.

 - Partner with design, content, and demand gen to bring events to life: landing pages, signage, swag, the full on-site experience.

 - Get a front-row seat on MaintainX's flagship client conference, with room to grow from logistics into programming.

Within your first 6–12 months, you'll be running smaller events solo and playing a real role in pulling off the flagship conference.

About You

Must-haves

 - 1–2+ years of experience in field marketing, event marketing, or a related in-person events role, ideally in B2B SaaS.

 - Experience executing in-person events, anything from small dinners to regional gatherings.

 - Strong project management skills and attention to detail; comfortable juggling multiple programs at once.

 - Excellent collaboration skills; you know how to work with Sales, vendors, and internal stakeholders to get things done.

 - A creative mindset and genuine enthusiasm for memorable, human-first experiences.

 - Valid passport and the ability to travel roughly 15% of the time across the US and Canada.

Nice-to-haves

 - Experience with CMMS, industrial software, or another startup / entrepreneurial environment.

 - Comfort with AI tools for day-to-day marketing work (nice to have, not required).

We Offer

 - Work that shows up in the physical world. What you help launch and promote keeps factories, fleets, and facilities running better.

 - Mentorship built in. You'll learn how to run a flagship client event from someone who already owns one, and get there faster for it.

 - Autodesk scale, same mission. Global reach and the resources of a public company, pointed at a problem we were already solving.

 - A career with real room. Field and events marketing is still being built out here, with a clear path from supporting the program to owning pieces of it outright.

Values & How We Work

We reward output, not hours logged or hats worn. You'll get real ownership as you grow into it, and a mentor invested in getting you there. We move fast, have honest conversations early, and expect the same back.

 Rejoignez une équipe des services de gestion des risques en pleine expansion et à fort impact au sein de laquelle votre expertise influencera directement la manière dont nous évaluons, gérons et atténuons les risques dans un large éventail de secteurs d’activité et de risques du domaine de l’assurance des entreprises.
 En tant qu’ingénieur(e) / conseiller(ère) principal(e) des risques, vous serez un(e) conseiller(ère) de confiance auprès des services de la souscription et de la gestion des demandes de règlement, des courtiers et des clients en leur proposant des conseils stratégiques en matière de gestion des risques et une expertise technique dans plusieurs catégories d’affaires.
 Vous contribuerez à soutenir une croissance rentable en cernant les facteurs de sinistres, en évaluant les risques émergents et en proposant des solutions pratiques et à valeur ajoutée d’atténuation des risques pour des comptes clients complexes, tant au Canada qu’à l’international.
 Ce que vous ferez 
 Diriger des évaluations des risques et fournir des services de conseil en matière de risques dans plusieurs branches de l’assurance des entreprises, notamment l’assurance de biens, l’assurance responsabilité civile, l’assurance environnementale, l’assurance risques divers, l’assurance de la responsabilité civile professionnelle, l’assurance de la responsabilité civile produits, l’assurance des parcs de véhicules et l’assurance des risques liés au secteur de la construction.
 Collaborer avec les équipes de souscription pour évaluer la qualité des risques, cerner les facteurs de sinistres et soutenir la stratégie de gestion des comptes, la tarification, la conservation des clients et les objectifs de croissance.
 Faire office de conseiller(ère) technique auprès des clients, des courtiers, des souscripteurs et des professionnels de la gestion des demandes de règlement concernant les pratiques exemplaires en matière de gestion des risques et les stratégies de prévention des sinistres.
 Élaborer et diffuser des recommandations techniques, des livres blancs, des programmes de formation et des initiatives de leadership éclairé portant sur les tendances et les risques émergents du secteur.
 Analyser les tendances en matière de sinistres au niveau des comptes, des secteurs d’activité et des portefeuilles afin de repérer les occasions permettant d’améliorer la sélection et l’atténuation des risques.
 Collaborer avec le réseau mondial de contrôle des risques de Liberty Mutual afin de partager des pratiques exemplaires et des solutions innovantes.
 Représenter Liberty Mutual lors de réunions avec des clients, d’examens de gestion responsable, d’événements organisés pour les courtiers, de conférences du secteur et au sein d’associations professionnelles.
 Encadrer vos collègues et contribuer au développement des compétences en contrôle des risques à l’échelle de l’organisation.

 Évaluation des risques et services de conseil

 Cerner les risques liés aux facteurs physiques, opérationnels et humains ainsi qu’aux systèmes de gestion susceptibles d’avoir une incidence sur les résultats en matière de sinistres.
 Évaluer les risques liés aux catastrophes naturelles, notamment les inondations, les tremblements de terre, les feux de forêt, les orages convectifs violents, le gel, les tempêtes de vent et les perturbations de la chaîne d’approvisionnement.
 Passer en revue les programmes relatifs à la continuité des activités, aux interventions d’urgence, à la gestion de crise et à la planification de la résilience.
 Évaluer les systèmes de protection contre les incendies, les programmes de gestion des défaillances, les pratiques d’entretien, les contrôles opérationnels et les cadres de gouvernance des risques.

BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cyber security SaaS portfolio.
 The Role 
 The Principal Software Security Architect owns security architecture for BeyondTrust's product suite end to end, including endpoint agents, thick clients, SaaS platforms, APIs, identity systems, and cloud-native services. This is an engineering leadership role embedded within Engineering and Architecture teams in the Office of the CTO, accountable for designing security into products from first principles through to what ships and runs in production, rather than reviewing other teams' work from the outside.
 We operate AI-first: Claude and LLM-driven workflows are how the team performs threat modeling, secure design reviews, vulnerability analysis, and developer enablement today, and this role is expected to operate at that level from day one and help extend that practice further. The ideal candidate brings 10+ years of hands-on software engineering and security architecture experience, deep expertise in threat modeling and attack surface reduction at scale, and practical experience applying LLM platforms to security engineering work.
 What You’ll Do 
 Own end-to-end security architecture for assigned product lines, from concept through production, defining the target-state architecture and secure-by-default patterns each product builds on.
 Lead threat modeling, attack surface analysis, and secure design reviews across products, platform services, endpoint agents, and cloud-native systems, driving the architectural decisions that eliminate unnecessary exposure rather than just documenting risk.
 Use LLM platforms (Claude, OpenAI) as core tools to scale threat analysis, abuse-case generation, architecture review, and remediation guidance, building the prompts, plugins, skills, and agent workflows that make the engineering org faster and more consistent.
 Embed secure-by-default patterns directly into product development, contributing reference architectures, reusable components, and automated guardrails, and building self-service security capabilities that let engineers make secure decisions without a bottleneck.
 Own and expand the Product Security handbook, a living system that feeds the team's AI workflows to enforce secure design standards, architecture guidance, and engineering best practices.
 Set technical direction for secure design across the org as a principal-level engineer, mentoring engineers, architects, and Security Champions on secure design, attack surface reduction, and AI-first security workflows.
 Help evolve BeyondTrust's AI-first Product Security Architecture strategy, identifying where AI workflows can replace manual processes, where they need human oversight, and where the next capability gaps are.
 What You’ll Bring 
 10+ years in Software Engineering, Security Architecture, Product Security, or Application Security, with a track record of owning architecture for shipping products
 Deep, practical experience with threat modeling, attack surface analysis, secure design reviews, and architecture risk analysis at scale, not just in theory
 Strong hands-on engineering background, with the ability to read and contribute to the codebase, design systems, and earn credibility with senior engineers as a peer
 Strong understanding of cloud-native systems, APIs, endpoint agents, thick clients, and identity/security platforms
 Hands-on experience using LLM platforms (Claude, OpenAI, or similar) in engineering or security workflows
 Ability to influence engineering and product teams from within, acting as a persuasive, credible, and practical partner rather than a gatekeeper
 Builder mindset, having created scalable security workflows, frameworks, or enablement programs, not just consumed them
 Experience building AI-native security workflows, plugins, agents, or developer tooling
 What Success Looks Like 
 Measurable reduction in product attack surface and recurring architecture risks, measured by risk eliminated, not findings produced
 Security architecture for owned product lines is defined, documented, and demonstrably adopted in shipping products
 Increased scale and consistency of secure design reviews through AI-first workflows
 Faster identification and remediation of design-level and architecture-level risks
 Engineering teams actively using self-service security capabilities that have been built
 Expansion of AI-first Product Security Architecture capabilities across the SDLC
 Nice To Have 
 Background in securing endpoint technologies, identity systems, or enterprise security platforms
 Offensive security experience or adversarial testing background
 Cloud security experience across AWS, Azure, or Kubernetes environments

In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking!

We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we:

 - Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform

 - Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour

 - Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use

We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build.

We are looking for Product Managers who can own the roadmap and strategy for the following areas:

 1. Product Platform: Ashby was designed from the beginning as a multi-product platform. We’re looking for a PM to establish this team and own the shared building blocks, foundational capabilities, and APIs that let product teams move quickly.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Bring strong technical product judgment and enjoy working on APIs, shared systems, and foundational capabilities
      
      - Know how to balance reusable building blocks with polished, customer-facing product experiences
      
      - Like creating leverage by helping teams ship quickly and consistently while improving what customers directly see and use

 2. AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context.
    
    - Great fit if you:
      
      - Have experience building AI-powered products, especially agents, copilots, or workflow automation
      
      - Enjoy shaping shared AI primitives like memory, context, orchestration, and evaluation
      
      - Can translate fast-moving AI capabilities into products that feel useful, reliable, and delightful

During the interview process, we’ll determine which role you're best suited for. We’re also advertising this opening as Staff Product Manager. Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience.

YOUR ROLE

 - Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity.

 - Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping.

 - Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months.

 - Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices.

 - Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges.

 - Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner across go-to-market teams to bring the features and products your team builds to the market. Anticipate and plan for the needs to help inform pricing, marketing, and customer support.

 - Ownership and reliability: follow through on commitments, manage time ruthlessly, respond promptly to stakeholders, and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change.

YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You have an unnatural curiosity and excitement about the end-user and the jobs they do

 - You bring an Engineering mindset to product problems and can think through edge cases and understand how to extend our underlying platform to create leverage

 - You can demonstrate taste - you care about the quality of the products you build and use

 - You're an excellent writer and synthesizer; you bring product knowledge and clarity to the entire organization and enable Engineers with product insights

 - You can build a thesis for prioritization and communicate priorities using a sound strategy that combines principled thinking, research, and data

 - You leverage tools and processes to build operational excellence into your product process

 - You have a strong business sense and understand how product and GTM should collaborate, how your features may be monetized, and how product priorities fit into larger business priorities

YOU MAY NOT BE A GREAT FIT IF

 - You prefer to specify exactly what Engineering should build rather than give engineers room to own the solution.

 - You dislike written documentation and prefer to manage the team via meetings and quick Slack messages.

 - You’re primarily interested in shipping features and not thinking through how to make them reusable platform capabilities.

 - You don’t enjoy doing deep research yourself and prefer to outsource that UX research, market research, and data teams.

 - You’re uncomfortable moving with urgency, making tradeoffs, and reprioritizing when new information emerges.

 - You’re primarily motivated by achieving a metric more than delivering a great product experience for customers.

WE WORK DIFFERENTLY

At Ashby, the role of Product Managers is different from what I’ve seen in most product orgs. At a high level, PMs are responsible for shipping impactful product changes at high velocity, consistently and over an extended period. When we think about impactful product changes, our primary goal is to remove frustration and add delight.

At many organizations, PMs are required to write detailed specs that handle every edge case. Designers are required to mock up every pixel. At Ashby, it’s different. We believe individual contributors do their best work when they have a deep understanding of the end user and the business, and ownership of the solution. This is reflected in the engineers Ashby hires: they own projects end-to-end and deeply understand the problems they are solving. PMs are expected to give significant white space in their specs. As a result, PMs can spend less time managing tickets and more time with customers and thinking deeply about the product strategy.

At Ashby, PMs need to be the pace-setters for their product areas. This means they bring a healthy level of impatience and time-paranoia to the table. This does not mean cutting corners or demanding that engineers work unreasonable hours. As a PM, you can help engineers by managing the project scope well, identifying when it’s appropriate to bring in help, or being ruthless about prioritization.

For PM roles at Ashby, we believe great products are built through deep thinking and a clear understanding of user needs. A major part of your role involves conducting thorough user research to uncover underlying customer problems and translating those insights into well-reasoned product strategies.

Finally, Ashby isn’t simply an ATS. Right from the foundations, it was designed to be much more than that. It’s a platform modelled around how organizations (from early-stage startups to massive enterprises) think about recruiting, managing, and retaining top talent. As a PM at Ashby, you should, over time, get familiar with our most common building blocks. You’ll invest not only in product improvements but in platform thinking.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates that advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect:

 1. Intro Call - 30 mins

 2. Product Experience Deep Dive - 1 hour

 3. Product Exercise - 1 hour

 4. Final Round Interview - 2 hours
    Mostly focused on cross-functional Interviews to meet more of the team. This is a critical hire for us and a role that will touch a lot of functions - we want to make sure you'll meet folks you'll be working closely with

BENEFITS

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets.

 - If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, which is also fully covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

To request reasonable accommodations, please contact hiring@ashbyhq.com.

Syntronic Production Services Canada is an Electronic Manufacturing Services provider located in Ottawa’s west end. Committed to our customers’ success, we understand that our people are our greatest asset, and we are always on the lookout for great talent.


The Production Engineering Director is responsible for the manufacturing process from new-product introduction through to stable, high-volume production. The role sets process standards, equipment strategy, and engineering methods so the factory launches products on time meeting, cost and quality targets.  Objectives include cost, throughput, and first-pass yield improvement year over year. Success is measured by NPI performance, process capability, equipment uptime, cost reduction, and the strength of the team.
Key responsibilities
Process ownership and capability
•    Own process design, documentation, and control for SMT operations, AOI, X-ray, selective and wave solder, conformal coating, press-fit, Box build, cable and harness, functional test, and final pack.
•    Define process, work instructions, visual standards, and control plans. Drive process capability (Cp/Cpk) on critical characteristics and close gaps with designed experiments
•    Lead root-cause analysis on yield loss, solder defects, component damage, test fallout, and escapes. Use structured problem solving (8D, fishbone, 5-Why, DOE) and deploy corrective actions into the process.
•    Maintain ESD, moisture-sensitive device, and cleanliness controls in line with IPC and customer requirements
New product introduction
•    Lead the plant NPI process from design-for-manufacturability review through pilot, first article, and release to volume. 
•    Run DFM and DFA reviews with design engineering. Challenge layouts, component choices, panelization, test access, and tolerances that will hurt yield or cycle time.
•    Own PFMEA, process flow, control plan, and work-instruction packages. Define inspection, AOI, and ICT/functional-test coverage with Quality and Test Engineering.
•    Manage prototype and pilot builds, first-article inspection, and customer or regulatory process qualifications. 
Equipment, automation, and capacity
•    Plan capital assembly equipment. Justify spend with capacity, quality, and labor models.
•    Own equipment acceptance, installation and process qualification.
•    Remove bottlenecks in SMT, 2nd Stage assembly, box build, test, and material kitting operations.
•    Set improvement objectives for the engineering teams in terms of uptime and throughput.
 Cost, yield, and continuous improvement
•    Own the engineering contribution for assembly cost: scrap, rework, consumables, labor content, and changeover efficiency. Publish yield reports as required.
•    Run structured improvement initiatives (lean, Six Sigma, etc) with operation teams to improve plant P&L and customer scorecards.
•    Standardize best practice processes across all lines and shifts.
Quality, compliance, and customer interface
•    Partner with Quality on IPC-A-610 / IPC-A-620 workmanship, J-STD-001 process control, IPC-7711/7721 rework limits, and customer-specific standards.
•    Support ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 27001, ISO14001, quality management systems.
•    Represent Production Engineering in customer visits, process audits, and failure investigations. 
•    Own traceability requirements with MES and ERP including component lot traceability, and test results tied to each board serial number.
People and organization
•    Lead and coach process, manufacturing and test engineers. 
•    Set technical standards, design rules, and review gates so junior engineers can make consistent decisions.
•    Build shift coverage and a response model for line-down events.
•    Recruit team members and develop successors for managers, team leads and principal-engineer roles. 
Qualifications
Required
•    P.Eng. accreditation, with Bachelor’s Degree in electrical, mechanical, industrial, manufacturing, or a related engineering discipline. 
•    Ten or more years in electronics assembly manufacturing, with at least five years leading process or manufacturing engineering.
•    Demonstrated ownership of board and box level assembly processes, including paste print, placement, reflow profiling, and inspection.
•    A record of taking products from NPI or transfer into stable volume production, with measurable yield and launch results.
•    Working knowledge of IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, and ESD (ANSI/ESD S20.20) requirements.
•    Experience leading engineers and influencing production, quality, supply chain, and design peers 
•    Ability to read schematics, assembly drawings, BOMs, and Gerber or ODB++ data well enough to challenge a process or a design.
Preferred
•    Master’s degree in engineering, with applied problem-solving credentials used on the factory floor.
•    Experience in a regulated or high-reliability environment: automotive (IATF 16949), medical (ISO 13485), aerospace (AS9100).
•    Hands-on exposure to ICT, flying probe, boundary scan, and functional test strategy, including fixture and coverage decisions.
•    Capital project leadership for new lines or a major capacity expansion, from specification through acceptance.
•    MES, ERP, SPC, and equipment-connectivity experience used to control processes, 
•    Experience with conformal coating, underfill, potting, press-fit and box-build of complete electronic products.
Working conditions
The role is based in the factory. A substantial share of time is on the production floor, in ESD-controlled areas, around reflow ovens, selective-solder equipment, and test cells. The director must be willing to support off-shift launches, customer audits, and line-down events. Occasional travel to customers, suppliers, and sister plants is expected.
This description covers the primary duties of the role. It is not an exhaustive list. Duties may be adjusted as products, volume, and plant structure change.

Hi! 👋 I'm Chris https://www.linkedin.com/in/chkrlee/, head of Product Design at Ashby.

We're looking for a versatile, intrinsically motivated designer who is excited to contribute to rethinking how modern software is designed. At Ashby, you'll be part designer, part product manager, part consultant, and part design system manager (or some combination of the 4!). We do design differently here, and if that excites you, read on.

Our unique approach is working - we're growing >100% year-over-year and have notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best-in-class among our peers: we have tens of millions in ARR, very low churn, and many years of runway. We're backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! We’ll share more details once we meet.

HOW WE WORK

In my previous roles, product teams always consisted of a product manager, a designer, and ~4-5 engineers. This may sound familiar to you! The product manager briefs the designer who then designs. After designing, mocks are handed to the engineers. 

We take a more principled approach here at Ashby. If you've been designing software enough, you'll realize in actuality, design is required in varying degrees on each project. Sometimes in the past, I'd be asked to design yet another settings page, when really all that was needed was an engineer to reuse existing components and just follow some documentation I had written. Other times, I felt I should effectively be the product manager and own a project from beginning to end. In these latter cases, it made sense that I was even the one providing project updates and managing resources rather than constantly being pinged by a separate product manager.

This principled approach is now what we do here, and it is part of what has allowed Ashby to take down incumbents in multiple verticals all at once. We don't settle for the status quo—we actively resist reversion to the mean.

Currently, I report to Benji, the co-founder & CEO. Both Abhik and Benji (our founders) care deeply about design, which at first glance may seem counterintuitive given the number of full-time designers that we employ. The belief is not that design is unimportant, but rather that it should be owned by the product team collectively, not solely by a group of full-time designers who happen to have the job title. 

The design department’s job at Ashby is not to make every single design decision but to equip our entire product team to make better decisions themselves, as well as edit decisions that PMs/Engineers choose to make. That, while tackling the biggest design challenges ourselves. 

Separate from design, you may also be excited by the fact that we maintain a near seed-stage-like culture with fuzzy lines between functional roles, as much autonomy as you can handle, and a focus on IC-work with an almost-no-meeting culture. While you get the product-market fit and scale of a growth-stage startup, you also get the agency and no-nonsense, no-red-tape culture of a seed-stage startup.

WHAT WE’RE BUILDING

Talent teams aspire to build a hiring process that identifies great candidates, moves them quickly through the interview process, and provides an excellent experience for the candidate. To accomplish this, recruiters perform thousands of daily tasks to coordinate and relay information between candidates, interviewers, and hiring managers. Teams struggle to keep up!

Scheduling a final round is an excellent example of our customers' challenges. A recruiter needs to collect availability from the candidate, identify potential interviewers, perform “Calendar Tetris” to find who is available to interview the candidate, schedule on the earliest date possible, and perform any last-minute adjustments as availability changes. They must perform this while considering the interview load on each individual and whether interviewers need to be trained and shadowing others. 

Ashby provides talent teams with intelligent and powerful software that provides insights into where they’re failing and automates or simplifies many of the tasks they’re underwater with. We put a lot of effort into designing products that are approachable to beginners but mastered and extended by power users. In many ways, spreadsheets set the bar here (and are what we often replace!).

WHY YOU SHOULD OR SHOULDN’T APPLY

YOUR QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 10+ years of product design experience, with the majority being in desktop SaaS

 - Able to take huge, ambiguous projects and break them down into actionable parts 

 - Able to speak to patterns of the highest functioning design teams and how to create an environment of high performance

 - Able to leverage designers' superpowers to influence engineering, product, and the rest of the company

 - Able to create standards and principles that will help improve the quality of design across the product org

 - Able to think from first principles instead of simply applying the “standard” UX processes.

 - Enough experience that your intuition can solve most usability problems without having to rely solely on data & metrics or conducting user research.

 - Curious & resourceful enough to come up with creative solutions and de-risk them appropriately.

 - Best-in-class skills in layout, navigation, IA, UI, and interaction design.

 - Obsession with craft & details.

 - You have experience at an early-stage startup or have spent time as a solo designer on a team.

YOU MAY WANT TO APPLY IF YOU’RE EXCITED ABOUT:

 - Creating leverage and impact far and above what you'd see in a typical EPD product team structure. You won’t be a cog in the wheel, the wheel is not very big!

 - Getting to work on all parts of a massive product surface area - spanning many user types, JTBDs, usability challenges, etc. Unlike in other organizations, you won’t be stuck working on one problem for many years.

 - Helping reinvent the design model for modern enterprise software—you don’t have to build wireframes, user journeys, personas, etc. What matters is solving a customer’s problem; what tools you use are up to you.

 - Covering all parts of the design process with a focus on design craft. You'll still be doing the occasional user research interview but will be focused on using heuristics & experience to improve our IA, navigation, interactions, UI patterns, and more.

 - Helping build our design system from (almost) the ground up.

CONVERSELY, YOU MAY NOT WANT TO APPLY IF:

 - You feel uncomfortable designing independently without much guidance from a PM or design management.

 - You’re uncomfortable having your decisions and process being challenged constantly by engineering & product.

 - You prefer an in-person role over remote (Ashby operates remotely).

 - You dislike written documentation.

 - You want a set structure and rhythm to your projects.
   
   - PM gives you a brief, you do wireframes, then mocks, then pass off work to engineers. Rinse and repeat.

 - You prefer a narrow job scope - interaction design only, design system only, etc.

ON A WEEKLY BASIS YOU WILL FIND YOURSELF:

 - Consulting for engineers who need help structuring layout, typography, flows, etc.

 - Digging into problems by consulting GTM, talking to customers, asking for data requests, and more in order to present confident assumptions about your proposals.

 - Using Figma to draw out your ideas and create visual artifacts for stakeholder alignment.

 - Writing specification docs (we call them specs!) that detail your design proposals. These documents are meant to get stakeholder alignment on the biggest decisions you want to make and are a core part of how we work at Ashby.

 - Taking ownership of larger product features and thinking through Jobs-To-Be-Done, navigation, information architecture, layout, interaction, etc.

 - Taking in customer feedback and using heuristics to build your own usability backlog and propose projects for engineers to take on.

 - Consolidating and refining our design system to be functional, aesthetic, and best-in-class.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

At Ashby, our team and interview process want to help you show your best self. We’ll dive into past projects and simulate working together and talking through decisions. Our interview process is four rounds with some casual Zoom coffee in between to get to know each other: 

 1. 30m introduction call to discuss Ashby and your experience

 2. 45m portfolio review

 3. 75m design exercise and app teardown. The exercise will be a live whiteboarding exercise where we provide a prompt and you show us how you'd break down problems and come up with solutions. 

 4. 2.5hr final round - meet the team + portfolio repeat with a founder

I'll be your main point of contact and prepare you for interviews. You’ll meet other engineers and product managers as well (with lots of time to ask them questions). If we don’t give an offer by the last round, I'll provide feedback as to why if you'd like it (I'm serious!).

BENEFITS

 - Competitive salary and equity.

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. This is one of the reasons I joined personally - not a lot of startups do this.

 - Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.

 - If you’re in the US, top-notch health insurance for you and your dependents with all premiums covered by us.

Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply.

ABOUT GEORGIAN



Georgian is a Toronto-based venture capital firm that partners with high-growth technology companies across cybersecurity, AI software, robotics, defense. We manage about $6B in assets and we have invested in more than 80 companies that we support with capital and technical capability.



Our in-house AI lab works directly with portfolio companies to provide a differentiated experience across the investment lifecycle, and drives the adoption of AI for our internal operations.

 


AI TECH LEAD - PHYSICAL AI & ROBOTICS



As a senior technical lead in Georgian’s AI Lab, you’ll work on the brain of the robot: the models it thinks with, the data it learns from, the simulators it practices in and the systems that get all of that onto real machines. The job has three parts: research what’s coming next, work inside our portfolio companies to get robot-learning systems from pilot into production and help our investment team judge physical AI companies. This is a software job. You won’t design actuators or own the hardware, but you’ll know enough about the body to understand what it will and won’t let the brain do.




WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS



Physical AI is a core investment thesis area for us. Our portfolio includes Bedrock Robotics, Path Robotics, Vention, and other frontier robotics companies. We think most of what separates these companies is the brain, not the body: how they collect and use data, the models that see and act, the world models and simulators they train against and the tools that get a new behavior from the lab onto a fleet of machines. That’s the part of the stack you’ll cover. You’ll track the latest trends in physical AI models and train physical AI systems yourself. You’ll know how a learned policy behaves on a real robot and what a working sim-to-real pipeline looks like. And you’ll be able to tell a system that’s really deployed from a good demo.




WHAT YOU’LL OWN & DELIVER



Edge Research: Working Out What’s Next. Keep up with what’s new in robot learning and work out what it means for the companies we back: VLAs, world models and WAMs, sim-to-real tooling and how to evaluate any of it properly. What you research turns into practical papers, tools, write-ups and advice.



Portfolio Acceleration: Hands-On Impact. Once we’ve invested, you’ll work inside portfolio companies to get robot-learning software from pilot into production: perception, RL policy training and fine-tuning, imitation learning, VLAs/WAMs, world models and simulation, data pipelines, evals and the on-robot inference and fleet tooling that keeps it all working in the field. You’ll work with CTOs and heads of autonomy on results they can measure: task success rate, how often someone has to intervene and how long it takes to stand up a new site.



Find & Win: Technical Due Diligence & Deal Flow. You’ll work with our investment team to look hard at physical AI companies, digging into each company’s autonomy stack, data and roadmap to answer the questions that matter. Is the autonomy learned or scripted? How reliably does it complete the task in messy, real-world conditions, and how often does a person have to step in once you’re past the demo? How long does it take to get a robot working at a new site or on a new task, and does each deployment produce data that makes the next one faster, or is every site a one-off integration? What’s hard to copy: the data, the models, the integration work or the hardware? What you find informs our view of the company, and you’ll talk directly with founders about what our AI Lab could build with them.




WE’RE LOOKING FOR




IDEAL ATTRIBUTES

 - 6+ years building production software; 3+ years leading ML projects, a good share of them on robots or other physical systems

 - You’ve put learned perception or policy models on real hardware that ran outside a lab: a warehouse, a factory floor, a field or a road

 - Deep knowledge of robot learning: imitation and reinforcement learning, VLA and world models, sim-to-real transfer and the data pipelines behind them

 - Solid software engineering: Python, plus enough C++ to read and debug an on-robot stack; ROS 2, real-time and on-device constraints, system design and DevOps

 - Enough hardware knowledge to work with mechanical, electrical and controls engineers as a peer, without having to do their jobs

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and with taking the lead, a clear writer and speaker




NICE-TO-HAVE



 - Time at a robotics or autonomy company that went from pilots to a deployed fleet, or on a big-tech or frontier-lab robotics team

 - Classical robotics as well as learning: motion planning, state estimation and control

 - Published work or real open-source contributions in robot learning (CoRL, RSS, ICRA, LeRobot or similar)

 - Experience in logistics, manufacturing, construction, agriculture or energy

 - You’ve founded a startup or joined one early, or built and grown an AI/ML team




CULTURAL ATTRIBUTES WE LOVE



 - Ambition and agency: You want to do big things and don’t wait to be told; you’re at your best with little structure and a lot of ownership

 - Curiosity: You chase problems to the root cause and keep asking “why,” even when the answer turns out to be a loose cable rather than the model

 - Team over ego: You make the people around you better, colleagues and founders alike

 - Plain talk: You can explain a hard technical thing briefly enough that a busy CEO gets it the first time

 - Builder: You’d rather ship a rough policy to a test cell today than a perfect one next quarter, and you know the difference between a demo and a deployment




WHAT WE OFFER



 - Competitive salary

 - Carried interest in Georgian’s funds

 - Health, dental and vision benefits

 - Flexible working

 - A budget for conferences and learning

 - The chance to publish research and represent Georgian at top robotics conferences



If you’ve ever watched a robot fail in the field and immediately wanted to know why, we’d love to hear from you.




POSITION STATUS



This posting represents an active, immediate vacancy on our team. We are currently interviewing for this role.



 


OUR COMMITMENT TO ACCESSIBILITY



Georgian is dedicated to building an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We provide reasonable accommodations throughout our recruitment process to ensure every candidate has the opportunity to perform at their best. If you require any specific accommodations at any stage, please reach out to us at peopleteam [at]  georgian.io.




USE OF AI



Innovation is at our core and we use artificial intelligence (AI) to support parts of our hiring process, such as screening and evaluating applications. These tools are designed to assist - not replace - human decision making and all final hiring decisions are made by our team.  We regularly review our AI tools to help promote fairness and reduce the risk of unintended bias. If you have any questions about how we use AI in our process or would like more information, please contact us at careers [at] georgian.io.

ABOUT THE ROLE?

Cohere’s Procurement team buys everything from pens to compute. We’re looking for a Lead, Direct Strategic Sourcing to own the categories closest to how we build: the technology, software, engineering talent and, over time, the compute that power our research and engineering teams.

You’ll put the structure in place so these buys scale with both speed and control, and as the function grows, you’ll hire and lead a small team of specialists and analysts.

OWN THE ENGINEERING AND R&D CATEGORIES

 - Own end-to-end strategic sourcing for Cohere’s engineering and R&D spend: technology licensing, OEM partnerships, engineering and IT software, developer and infrastructure tooling, and engineering staff augmentation and services.

Who we are
 Unit8, founded in 2017, is a high-tech, dynamic Swiss leader in AI and data analytics consulting, renowned for solving complex challenges in non-digital native industries such as automotive, chemicals, financial services, manufacturing, and pharma. Our partnerships with industry leaders like Palantir, NVIDIA, and OpenAI underscore our commitment to excellence. With over 300 successful projects and a team of ~200 professionals across Switzerland, Poland, Germany, Spain and the US, we have entered the Canadian market in early 2026 and are set for further expansion.
 Our mission
 Unit8 is dedicated to driving AI adoption in non-digital industries and accelerating their digital transformation. We invest in projects that matter, including pro-bono initiatives and “engineering for good” causes.
 The opportunity
 Following our growth in Europe and our recent expansion into the US market in early 2026, Unit8 is taking its next strategic step in North America. We are looking for a commercially minded Head of Legal to help establish our Canadian presence in Montréal and to be the senior legal voice for our North American business.
 This is, above all, a business-enabling role. You are the person who sits with our sales, delivery and finance teams, understands what a deal needs to succeed, and turns complex legal risk into clear, practical positions that help us close. You are the bridge between our clients’ legal and procurement teams and our own business, fluent enough in both to protect Unit8 without slowing it down.
 You own the contracting and legal strategy for Canada and the US. You negotiate our client and purchasing agreements, decide what is handled in-house and what goes to external counsel, and build a modern, AI-enabled contract review process. Reporting directly to our CFO, you also lead our junior In-house Legal Counsel in Europe and act as the escalation point for contract reviews across our other geographies.
 As one of our first Canadian hires, you will help shape how Unit8 contracts in North America, which standards and playbooks we work from, and how our legal function scales as we grow.
 What you'll do
 As our Head of Legal, you will be the senior legal voice for Unit8 in North America. Based in our Montreal office and reporting directly to our CFO in Europe, you will own commercial, procurement and governance legal work for our Canadian and US business, and lead a small, global legal function. This is a hands-on role with real ownership: you’ll close deals, shape how we contract, and build a modern, AI-enabled legal process from the ground up.
 Close the deals that grow our North American business 
 Review, draft and negotiate client contracts: MSAs, SOWs, NDAs, data processing agreements, IP and licensing terms, subcontracting and partnership agreements, as well as purchasing contracts.
 Lead face-to-face and remote negotiations with client legal and procurement teams, preparing the negotiation strategy, fallback positions and risk assessment for every material deal.
 Advise our sales, delivery and finance teams on liability caps, indemnities, IP ownership and data protection, in plain language they can act on.
 Own our Canadian and US contract templates, playbooks and standard positions: learn them quickly, improve them where needed, and use them to build client proposals and contracts.
 Work alongside our DPO and CISO on data protection topics.
 Keep our North American entities in good shape 
 Prepare and maintain corporate governance documents for our Canadian and US entities.
 Support the CFO and the board on corporate structure matters.
 Decide what stays in-house and what goes out 
 Route matters to external counsel in Canada, the US or Europe when it makes sense, weighing urgency, complexity and cost.
 Select, brief and manage external counsel, own the external legal budget and review invoices against scope.
 Lead and grow the legal team 
 Manage and coach our junior In-house Legal Counsel based in Europe : set priorities, allocate work and review output across time zones.
 Act as backup reviewer for EU and MEA contracts when our European counsel is at capacity.
 Report to the CFO on workload, open matters, material contractual risks and external legal spend.
 Build an AI-enabled legal function 
 Run and continuously improve our end-to-end contract review process: intake, triage, turnaround targets, approval thresholds and sign-off.
 Govern and develop AI tools for first-pass review, clause comparison and redlining, with clear rules on confidentiality, human sign-off and quality control. You’ll be working at an AI company, so expect to put these tools to real use.
 Track review volumes and turnaround times and use the data to make the process faster and better.
 To be clear on scope: employment and labour law, as well as litigation and dispute resolution, are not part of this role and remain with HR and external counsel.
 Who you are
 You hold a law degree and are a member in good standing of the Barreau du Québec (or another Canadian law society with eligibility to practise in Quebec).
 You bring 7–10 years of experience as legal counsel in commercial and corporate law, in-house or at a law firm or legal service provider.
 You have negotiated services agreements, SOWs and software terms in an IT, SaaS or professional services company.
 You’re confident with Quebec civil law and the common-law framework of the other provinces, particularly Ontario.
 You have a working knowledge of US commercial contract law: you can work from our US templates, spot issues and know when to bring in US counsel. (You won’t be practising US law.)
 You’re familiar with Quebec Law 25, PIPEDA and, at a basic level, US state privacy laws.
 You have managed at least one direct report or a small team, and you enjoy developing people.
 You’re fully bilingual in French and English, and comfortable negotiating and drafting in both languages.
 You have built or redesigned a legal intake and review process, and you measure turnaround and quality.
 You read contracts for their business impact on margin, cash and delivery risk, not only for legal exposure.
 You’re curious about AI in legal work: you use these tools, understand their limits, and know how to govern them responsibly.
 You thrive working autonomously as the only lawyer in your region, while staying closely connected to a team in Europe.
 Language 
 Unit8 operates as one international team across Switzerland, Poland, Germany and now North America, and works with global clients. English is therefore our day-to-day working language across the company and within delivery teams. For this role, professional fluency in both English and French is required.
 What we offer
 The chance to be the first senior legal hire in North America and shape how Unit8 contracts across the region, with direct access to our CFO and leadership.
 Real impact: your work directly enables projects that bring AI and data science to some of the largest companies in traditional industries.
 A modern legal function where AI tools are part of the daily workflow, not an afterthought.
 Flexible working: 30–40 hours per week to be agreed with you, with at least 2–3 days per week in our Montreal office and the rest remote. Your day starts by 8:00 or 9:00 AM Eastern to overlap with our European colleagues.
 Occasional travel to client sites in Canada and the US, and regular visits to our European offices.
 A collaborative, international team of 150+ engineers, data scientists and consultants who care about doing great work, including pro-bono and “engineering for good” projects.

 Leadership and Team Development

 Performance and Continuous Improvement

 Quality Systems and Compliance

Who are we?

Our mission is to scale intelligence to serve humanity. We’re training and deploying frontier models for developers and enterprises who are building AI systems to power magical experiences like content generation, semantic search, RAG, and agents. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. We like to work hard and move fast to do what’s best for our customers.

Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are passionate about their craft. Each person is one of the best in the world at what they do. We believe that a diverse range of perspectives is a requirement for building great products.

Join us on our mission and shape the future!



Why this role?

We are on a mission to build machines that understand the world and make them safely accessible to all. Data quality is foundational to this process. Machines (or Large Language Models to be exact) learn in similar ways to humans - by way of feedback. By labelling, ranking, auditing, and correcting text output, you will improve Large Language Model’s performance for iterations to come, thus having a lasting impact on Cohere’s tech.


Cohere seeks dynamic and dedicated Data Annotators with exceptional Modern Standard German Writing, Translation, and Data Manipulation skill.



Please Note: This is a part-time independent contractor position available within Canada. We seek candidates who are able to commit to 16 hours per week minimum at a 30 CAD/hour contract rate. This role is BYOD 💻 - Bring Your Own Device (laptop). Remote work within Canada. 12 months contract. Performance incentives included!



As a Data Annotation Specialist, you will:

 - Label and Rank: Accurately label and rank machine learning data with advanced proficiency in German, ensuring data integrity and quality.

 - Audit and Correct: Scrutinize and rectify any inaccuracies in language data (may include text, image, JSON, TSV/CSV, Markdown), maintaining the highest standard of data accuracy.

 - Reading and Text-Based Tasks: Efficiently complete reading and text-based assignments, with high attention to detail.

 - Preference-Based Tasks: Evaluate and complete tasks, assessing which responses in German best conform to project guidelines.

 - Recommend Optimizations: Identify and suggest opportunities for improving data quality and model performance in German language tasks.

 - Provide Feedback: Collaborate and communicate effectively, providing feedback to cross-functional team members, particularly on German language-related matters.

 - Detail-Oriented Execution: Maintain meticulous attention to detail while performing repetitive and precise tasks, particularly when working with language data.



You may be a good fit if you have:

 - Language Proficiency: Native or near-native proficiency in German; excellent command over English.

 - Expert reading and writing skills - which you are ready to prove on our written test.

 - Basic familiarity with JSON/TSV/CSV/Markdown data manipulation.

 - Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy - you’re the type to proofread all of your emails!

 - High tolerance for repetitive and monotonous work.

 - Ability to follow complex instructions, navigate ambiguity and work independently.

 - Superb sense of urgency and time management.

 - Curiosity about technology and a knack for tackling problems in creative ways.

 - A reliable laptop.



The Candidate Journey:
Initial Screening - Once you have submitted your application our Talent Team will review your resume and writing samples.
Virtual Annotation Test -  This assignment will test your written skill through various language-based tasks, such as a a writing sample, interacting with a chat bot, and more.
Video Screen - If selected to move forward, you will have a short video call with a member of our Operations Team!
Offer - Independent Contractor Agreement


As an independent contractor, you maintain control over how you complete your work and may work with multiple clients simultaneously, although we ask you to declare if any of these are with a direct competitor of Cohere and maintain IP confidentiality of the Cohere project. Independent contractors are not eligible for health benefits or other benefits provided to employees. Compensation for services is provided to contractors by contractors invoicing for services provided pursuant to the terms of our agreement with the contractor.

It is important to understand that as an independent contractor, continuous work is not guaranteed. The client-contractor relationship is fundamentally project-based, meaning engagements may be temporary, periodic, or intermittent based on our organizational needs and project availability. As an independent contractor, you should anticipate fluctuations in workflow and therefore compensation for services when Cohere does not require as many hours of services in a week.

Prospective candidates, please be advised: this role involves working with human generated and model generated tasks that may involve exposure to not safe for work (NSFW) text content as part of data annotation tasks, including explicit, offensive, or other inappropriate material.

ABOUT REMARCABLE

Remarcable builds the software that keeps trade contractors' crews equipped and on schedule. Our platform brings material procurement, inventory and tool tracking, prefab requisitions and invoice automation into one place, connecting field crews, warehouses, purchasing teams and suppliers in real time. We were founded by former foremen, purchasers, project managers and engineers who lived the jobsite pain we now solve, and today we serve more than 40% of the top 50 electrical contractors in the U.S.

Backed by a $15M Series A led by Insight Partners (June 2025), we are growing fast across our teams in the U.S. and Vancouver, B.C. That growth is why we are hiring for this role.

THE ROLE

As our AI Engineer, you will turn the data flowing through Remarcable every day (purchase orders, quotes, invoices, inventory and supplier catalogs) into AI features that save contractors real hours. You will design, build and ship LLM-powered capabilities into our product and internal tools, from intelligent invoice matching and document extraction to an AI assistant that answers questions on top of our new data lakehouse. You will report to the VP of Engineering and work side by side with our Product, Data and Full Stack Engineering teams.

This is a hands-on, builder role at a company where AI is still being defined. One week you may prototype a retrieval pipeline or an agent that drafts a purchase order; the next you may harden it for production, set up evaluations, or explain to a customer how it works. You will help set the patterns, tools and guardrails that every future AI feature at Remarcable is built on.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

BUILD AI INTO THE PRODUCT

 - Design, build and ship LLM-powered features across the platform, such as invoice and PO matching, quote and document extraction, catalog normalization and smart purchasing suggestions.

 - Build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and agentic workflows that act on real procurement, inventory and accounting data.

 - Own features end to end: prototype, production rollout, monitoring and iteration based on customer feedback.

DATA, RETRIEVAL AND INFRASTRUCTURE

 - Partner with our Data Engineering team to use the data lakehouse as the foundation for AI features and an internal AI assistant.

 - Build and maintain embedding pipelines, vector search and the APIs that serve AI features to our web and mobile apps.

 - Integrate with leading model providers (e.g., Anthropic, OpenAI) and choose the right model for each job based on quality, latency and cost.

QUALITY, SAFETY AND RELIABILITY

 - Create evaluation sets and automated tests so we can measure accuracy before and after every change.

 - Monitor AI features in production for accuracy, cost, latency and drift, and fix issues quickly.

 - Put guardrails in place for data privacy, security and customer trust, supporting our ISO and compliance work.

PARTNER ACROSS THE COMPANY

 - Work with Product Managers to find the workflows where AI saves contractors and suppliers the most time.

 - Help Customer Success, Support and internal teams automate manual work with AI tools.

 - Share what you learn through documentation, demos and code reviews, and raise the AI fluency of the whole engineering team.

PROJECTS THAT HELP US SCALE

 - Lead or support projects such as AI-assisted AP automation, a natural-language assistant for our customers, and AI-powered supplier onboarding.

 - Bring ideas, raise risks and pitch in wherever the team needs it.

WHAT YOU BRING

REQUIRED

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, including at least 1–2 years building and shipping LLM or machine learning features to production.

 - Strong Python skills and experience building production APIs and services.

 - Hands-on experience with LLM APIs, prompt design, RAG, embeddings and vector databases (e.g., pgvector, Pinecone, OpenSearch).

 - Experience building evaluations and measuring model quality, not just demos.

 - Solid SQL and data skills; comfortable working with messy, real-world business data.

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS preferred), CI/CD and observability.

 - Clear communication skills and the ability to explain AI trade-offs to non-technical teammates and customers.

 - A builder's mindset: comfortable with ambiguity, quick to create structure, and happy to do both strategic and hands-on work.

 (Read this whole thing. If you quit halfway, we already have your answer.) 
 Most job ads read like they were written by HR. 
Bullet points. Buzzwords. 
A "competitive compensation package" that translates to "we'll pay you just enough to keep you from leaving, but never enough to actually win." 
 This isn't that.
 This is a letter. From us to you. About one of the most lopsided opportunities we've ever put in front of a salesperson and the rare, specific human being we're trying to find to fill it.
 If that human is you, you're going to feel it in your chest somewhere around paragraph nine.
 First — Who We Are. And Why It Matters. 
 We're Wealth Without Wall Street. 
 Russ Morgan and Joey Muré built this from scratch, not in a Manhattan glass tower, not with a hedge-fund pedigree, but by getting fed up watching hardworking business owners hand their financial futures to suit-wearing strangers who couldn't pick them out of a lineup.
 Together we've helped thousands of business owners, real estate investors, doctors, and high-earning professionals do what 99% of America has been brainwashed into believing is impossible:
 Generate passive income that exceeds their monthly expenses. 
 That's the whole game. That's what freedom actually looks like — not a 401(k) you can't touch until you're 65 and your knees are gone, but real cash flowing in every single month whether you work or not.
 We do it using the Infinite Banking Concept — the same wealth strategy quietly used by the richest families in America for over a century. We teach people to become their own bank. To recycle their capital. To stop renting money from institutions that profit off their ignorance.
 Russ and Joey have done it themselves. Over $50,000 per month in passive income. Co-authors of an Amazon bestseller. Hosts of one of the most respected podcasts in personal finance.
 This isn't theory. This is the real thing.
 Right now, we have more qualified people waving their hands than we can possibly talk to.
 That's where you come in.
 The Role: Business Developer. (Translation: The Person Who Decides Who Gets Free.) 
 Let us describe a typical day so you know exactly what you're signing up for.
 You wake up. You check your calendar. There are real, pre-qualified humans on it, people who registered for our workshops, devoured Russ and Joey's content, raised their hand, and said "I want a Passive Income Game Plan Session." 
 These aren't cold strangers. 
These aren't leads scraped off a list. 
These are people who already trust the brand, already believe the philosophy, and already know they're tired of the rat race.
 Your job is to pickup the phone, set appointments by making outbound calls and take inbound appointments.
Ask the kind of questions most salespeople are too soft to ask. 
Find out where they really are financially, emotionally, mentally. Diagnose whether IBC and our path is actually right for them.
 And if it is? You hand them the keys.
 You're not pitching. You're not pressuring. You're not chasing.
 You're the bridge between someone's current life — exhausted, overworked, financially fragile — and the version of their life where they sleep through the night because money is finally working for them instead of against them.
 That's the job.
 If that sounds like too much responsibility, the back button is right there.
 Who We Are NOT Looking For. 
 Let's save us both some time.
 We are not looking for the guy who calls himself a "closer" because he sold timeshares in Cabo for six months.
 We are not looking for the person who needs a six-week ramp, a personal coach, three resource Slack channels, and a "psychologically safe" environment to dial a phone.
 We are not looking for someone who's going to ghost on Friday afternoons because the surf is up.
 We are not looking for a salary chaser. If a guaranteed paycheck is what you're after, McDonald's is hiring. Go thrive.
 And we are definitely not looking for someone who can't speak from the heart about money, freedom, and the very real fear most Americans carry around about both. If you can't connect at the soul level, you can't sell this. Period.
 Who We ARE Looking For. 
 A killer. But a killer with a conscience.
 Someone who can sit across a Zoom screen from a stranger and — within ten minutes — have them admitting things they haven't told their spouse.
 Someone who's already a top performer somewhere else and is bored to tears selling SaaS, solar, or something else they couldn't care less about.
 Someone who reads Rich Dad Poor Dad , listens to BiggerPockets, follows Dave Ramsey just to argue with him, and already has an opinion about whole life insurance — even if that opinion needs updating.
 Someone with the spine to say "I don't think you're a fit. Here's why," and walk away from money on principle.
 Someone who treats every conversation like it's their last shot — because that's how the great ones do it.
 If you read those five paragraphs and felt seen, keep going.
 The Non-Negotiables.
 Proven sales background. Minimum 2+ years closing in a high-ticket, phone/Zoom-based environment. We don't care about your resume — we care about your numbers.
 25%+ close rate after probation. Below that, you're not the right fit and we'll part as friends.
 Full ownership of your pipeline. Nobody is going to chase you to follow up. The leads are there. The CRM is built. The systems work. You just have to work them. 
 Show up sharp every single day. This is a high-tempo environment. We move. We measure. We adjust.
 Live the message. If you don't believe building wealth outside the traditional system is possible, you cannot sell it. Period. Bonus points if you already own a whole life policy, have read Becoming Your Own Banker by Nelson Nash, or have personal experience with real estate investing or passive income.
 Stable, professional remote setup. High-speed internet, quiet environment, quality camera and mic. We're representing a premium brand on every single call.
 CRM discipline. You log notes the same day. You update statuses in real time. If "I forgot to update the CRM" is a phrase that comes out of your mouth more than twice, this won't work.
 Emotional intelligence over scripts. We'll give you frameworks. We will not give you a robot script to memorize. If you can't read a human, you can't sell here.
 Coachable ego. Strong opinions, loosely held. We promote killers who listen. We fire prima donnas who don't.
 A worldview that aligns. You believe people are responsible for their own freedom. You believe Wall Street is not the answer for most families. You believe in earning the right to be paid well — not waiting to be handed it.
 The Catch: 
 We get a lot of applications. 
Most won't make it past the first filter. 
We're not looking for a resume, we're looking for evidence. 
 A sales background that proves you can sit in the fire without flinching, a track record that doesn't need to be inflated, and a worldview that aligns with what we actually believe about money, freedom, and the responsibility of helping someone change their life.
 If that's you, apply. Right now. While you're feeling it.

 Sound familiar?
 That's right. 
We pay you the same way we teach our clients to live. 
Passive income. Compounding. Freedom.
 If we wouldn't drink our own Kool-Aid with the people who sell our offer, we'd have no business selling it to anyone.
 What's In It For The Right Person. 
 Beyond the money?
 Mission that matters. You'll be the first conversation thousands of families ever have about real financial freedom. You'll be the one who makes them realize they've been lied to for thirty years, and you'll be the one who shows them the way out.
 Direct access to Russ Morgan and Joey Muré, two of the most generous, mission-driven, real-deal humans in this industry.
 Elite-level sales coaching from closers who've done eight figures in this exact niche.

 Pre-qualified, warm inbound leads — not cold lists, not scraped data, not random dials.
 A real product you can be proud of. No bait-and-switch. No fake scarcity. No "course that goes nowhere." A genuine pathway to freedom backed by a decade of results.
